wv_piney_creek_watershed.blurb: A young sandstone crag in the Piney Creek Gorge outside Beckley, roughly half an hour south of the main New River Gorge cliffs. It holds 22 routes, mostly bolted lines with a handful of trad climbs, and the grades run from easy fives up into the low 5.12s, with a fair number of 5.9 to 5.11 lines in the middle. The stone is mixed: some sections are hard and clean, others are softer with iron banding and pockets, and loose rock turns up while development continues, so a helmet is wise. It was built with beginners and students in mind, and fixed teaching anchors make it a handy place to learn. Expect a walk of about twenty minutes in.

wv_10_savory_area.blurb: A short sandstone cliff band in the Bozoo crags, on the New River in southern West Virginia. The 22 routes are almost all trad or top-rope, with a couple of dedicated top-ropes, and the grades cluster around 5.8 to 5.11 with the bulk of them in the 5.9 range. Lines are roughly 40 to 50 feet tall and many follow tidy cracks, so it suits a modest rack and a day of moderate crack practice. The wall looks west to southwest and collects warm light through the afternoon. The cliff sits directly above a boulder field, and the broader Bozoo zone is quiet and seldom crowded.

wv_j_snake_buttress.blurb: The central stretch of Endless Wall in the New River Gorge, and often called its best-quality section. It has 22 routes, mainly sport (15) with six trad lines and a single aid line. Difficulty starts around 5.9 and builds quickly: a few 5.10s, then a big cluster of 5.11 to 5.13 face climbs on hard sandstone, topping out near 5.14. This is a strong choice for a climber with solid 5.11 sport mileage rather than a beginner. The wall takes a lot of direct sun, so it is more pleasant in spring and fall than in summer heat. You reach it by descending a fixed ladder system from the rim and traversing upstream.

wv_roof_rocks.blurb: A small sandstone cliff in Coopers Rock State Forest near Morgantown, set close to the old iron furnace. About 22 problems and routes are spread across short roped climbs, a few leads and some boulder problems. Most roped lines sit in the easy to moderate range, with a few harder trad and top-rope pitches, while the boulder problems stretch from V1 to V10. Walls run about 40 to 50 feet, tall by local standards, and overhanging roof features give the place its name. Because the cliff top is easy to reach and anchors can be built from trees, it is a popular spot for first-time top-roping and instruction, so expect groups on busy days.

wv_g_diamond_point.blurb: A prominent cliff on Endless Wall in the New River Gorge, easy to pick out when you look across the canyon from the big bridge. It carries 22 routes, with more trad (13) than sport (9). Grades begin near 5.7 but most lines sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with one 5.13, so it rewards a climber comfortable on harder gear routes and bolted faces. The rock is sandstone, and since the ground above the rim rises and sends no runoff over the edge, the wall tends to dry quickly after rain. The way down is a single-rope rappel from the top, and a large boulder at the base can fool you into stopping early.

wv_rhodo_cave.blurb: A well-loved bouldering cave on the Rhododendron Trail in Coopers Rock State Forest, near Morgantown. All 22 problems are boulder problems on the gritty, quartz-rich sandstone typical of the forest, which means slopers, rounded jugs and shallow pockets, and plenty of stiff grades. The spread is broad: a few easy V1s, a solid middle at V3 to V5, and a steady run of hard problems from V6 into the V10s and V11. The cave is known for staying dry in rain and rarely seeps, which makes it a reliable bad-weather option, apart from condensation on hot summer days. Bring pads and plan a short hike down the trail from the parking pull-off.

wv_5_white_wall.blurb: A tall, light-colored sandstone wall in the Kaymoor section of the New River Gorge, near Fayetteville. It holds 22 routes, about 13 sport and nine trad. The climbing is steep and sustained: only a couple of lines are 5.9, a handful are 5.10, and the great majority fall in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, with two reaching 5.13. Shade is the big draw here, making it a comfortable summer option when neighboring cliffs are crowded or hot, and several of its hard sport lines stay dry through rain. The trail from the parking lot follows the approach used by the nearby busy crag, then cuts across to the left, taking about 10 to 15 minutes.

wv_3_greatest_show_area.blurb: A compact, high-quality cliff on the Lower Meadow in the Meadow River Gorge, a short drive from the New River Gorge. The 22 routes split between sport (12) and trad (10), and the grades lean hard: one 5.9, a few 5.10s and 5.11s, then a long run of 5.12 and 5.13 lines and one 5.14. Big roofs and a vivid yellow and orange headwall define the wall, and the area has few moderate sport lines, so it suits strong climbers. Many of the lines stay dry in the rain. Reaching it means a walk of 5 to 10 minutes on an ATV track, followed by a climbers' path up to the base.
